title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization overhead, thread-pinning and threadpool improvements
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Reduced CPU p50 request latency by 12-18% on mixed workloads by optimizing request serialization, reducing threadpool contention, and adding optional thread pinning. No behavioral API changes.
description: Motivation: Production traces and perf lab runs showed significant CPU-side overhead in the request path for short requests (<=64 tokens). Root causes: repeated small serializations, threadpool contention on high QPS, and cross-socket thread migration increasing scheduler latency. This PR addresses these by: 1) replacing ad-hoc serialization with a fast, preallocated sbuffer path for common request shapes, avoiding extra heap allocations and temporary strings; 2) refactoring request worker threadpool to use a bounded MPSC queue and a light-weight work-stealing fallback to reduce lock contention under bursty loads; 3) adding optional CPU thread pinning for worker threads with sensible defaults (per-socket pinning) and exposing configuration via REDWOOD_CPU_AFFINITY env var and runtime flag; 4) moving non-critical bookkeeping (metrics aggregation, trace formatting) off the hot path to a dedicated background aggregator thread; 5) adding pinsafe guards for containers/isolated environments and falling back to no-affinity when capabilities are missing. The change is opt-in for thread pinning (disabled by default) but serialization and queue improvements are safe defaults. Measured improvements: - p50 latency improvement: 12% on small-sync workload (local perf-lab) - p95 latency improvement: 8% under mixed-sequence workload - CPU utilization for same QPS reduced by ~9% Benchmarks and tracing attached in the CI run. See linked Linear ENG-1976 for rollout plan and ENG-2042 for KB/monitoring tasks. Checklist: - [x] fast-path sbuffer implementation + unit tests - [x] threadpool refactor + integration tests - [x] thread pinning feature + env/runtime flag - [x] metrics/tracing for scheduler latency - [x] documentation for configuration and known limits Changeset summary: see commits below. Merge strategy: squash merge to keep history concise. Rollout plan: feature gated thread affinity, staged rollout on Dedicated then Hosted, fall back to no-affinity if perf regressions seen.
commits: squash: implement fast sbuffer serializer and replace ad-hoc JSON serialization (M. Thompson)
refactor: replace global threadpool with bounded queue + work-stealing fallback (M. Thompson)
feat: optional thread pinning support and config via REDWOOD_CPU_AFFINITY (M. Thompson)
chore: add scheduler latency metrics and perf tests (M. Thompson)
docs: runtime config and rollout notes (M. Thompson)
test: perf harness scripts for small/medium/large prompt mixes (M. Thompson)
diff_snippets: serving/runtime/request_serializer.cpp: add SBuffer fast-path that preallocates 512B and serializes common fields with memcpy to avoid std::string temporaries
serving/runtime/thread_pool.cpp: swap std::deque+mutex for bounded MPSC queue + light work-stealing (worker-local queue) and reduce lock holds around push/pop
serving/runtime/affinity.cpp: new optional API that reads REDWOOD_CPU_AFFINITY and pins worker threads using sched_setaffinity on linux; no-op on unsupported platforms
serving/metrics/scheduler_metrics.cpp: move trace formatting out of hot path and aggregate histograms on aggregator thread
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice reduction in allocations — can we make the sbuffer size heuristics configurable? Author: Added REDWOOD_SBUFFER_SIZE env var and runtime override; default 512B should cover 80% of requests.

Priya Rao: Thread pinning looks good but worried about noisy neighbor on multi-tenant hosts. Author: Pinning is off by default; rollout plan recommends enabling only on Dedicated pools and in perf lab first.
Liam Nguyen: CI flaked on one perf test initially. Author: Re-ran perf harness after fixing timing dependency in test; CI green now.
Ethan Cole: Can you add a metric for 'thread_migrations' to detect cross-socket steals? Author: Added scheduler.thread_migrations counter in this PR.
Ops (automated): Please update deploy docs for affinity. Author: deploy/docs/affinity.md added with caveats and troubleshooting.
notes_on_rollback: Thread pinning is feature-gated and can be disabled via runtime flag without redeploy. If serialization path causes issues, revert to previous serializer by toggling REDWOOD_USE_FAST_SBUFFER=false at runtime.

Monitor host-level CPU steal and cross-socket migrations during rollout
notes: This PR focuses on CPU path. Future work: consider moving serializer into SIMD-accelerated path and extend pinning policy to isolate IO vs compute threads on multi-socket systems.
